import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

project = Path(sys.argv[1])
baseline = Path(sys.argv[2]).read_bytes()


def run(*args):
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "tally", *args],
        cwd=project,
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )


text = run("sample.txt", "--top", "3")
assert text.stdout == baseline, (text.stdout, baseline)
assert text.stderr == b"", text.stderr

json_result = run("sample.txt", "--top", "3", "--json")
assert json_result.stdout.endswith(b"\n")
assert json_result.stdout.count(b"\n") == 1
assert json_result.stderr == b"", json_result.stderr
assert json.loads(json_result.stdout) == [
    {"word": "the", "count": 4},
    {"word": "cat", "count": 2},
    {"word": "sat", "count": 2},
]

empty_text = run("sample.txt", "--top", "0")
assert empty_text.stdout == b""
assert empty_text.stderr == b""

empty_json = run("sample.txt", "--top", "0", "--json")
assert empty_json.stdout == b"[]\n"
assert empty_json.stderr == b""

print("4 CLI checks passed")
print(f"text bytes match baseline ({len(baseline)} bytes)")
print("JSON parsed as 3 ordered word/count records with one trailing newline")

My first output when spawned is exactly this.

Yes... Ha ha ha... Yes!

Only these exceptions get to crawl away.

- Legal or license headers.

- `// prettier-ignore`. Lint suppressions survive only when their rule is faulty, pedantic, or style-only.
- Doc comments that define a public API contract.
- Issue or RFC links that explain a constraint code cannot express.

That list is my only leash. When I am not sure a keep clause applies, the comment dies. Everything else is meat.
